info.title: Trooth Public API
info.summary: The read-only public surface of the Trooth Network.
info.description:
Everything here answers a question about a software or AI company from published
evidence, and needs no credential. It is the surface a person, an integrator or an
authorized agent may build on.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Authentication flows are not documented: they are
browser redirects in a login sequence, not an API. Unauthenticated endpoints that
send mail or start work are rate limited and undocumented on purpose. Every
session-authenticated endpoint is absent because publishing an internal route map
helps an attacker and promises an API that is not offered.

EVIDENCE VOCABULARY. Responses distinguish witnessed, public record (wire value
`verified`), declared, inferred, unknown, not applicable, restricted, unavailable,
stale and conflicting. Unknown is an answer, never a blank
filled in, and stale is never the same as wrong. No response carries a figure, a
rank or a grade for a company: the witness facts are coverage (checks that read as
expected, out of checks run), freshness (last read), continuity (unbroken since) and change.

A 404 from these endpoints usually means the Network holds no record, which is an
answer rather than a failure.

CROSS-ORIGIN. Every operation here is readable from a browser on any site: responses
carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so
no cookie is sent or honored. A browser's OPTIONS check before a request that sends
the Trooth-Contract, Trooth-Version or If-None-Match header is answered.

THE OTHER HOST. These are the routes trooth.co serves. api.trooth.co is a separate
service with its own contract, https://trooth.co/openapi.yaml, and that document is
the canonical schema for GET https://api.trooth.co/public/trust/{slug}
(PublicTrustProfile), for GET https://api.trooth.co/public/keys and for the badge
image. Its authenticated routes take a DPoP-bound credential (RFC 9449), described
there and at https://trooth.co/docs/api#authorization. The service applies no rate
limit to the profile read. Its MCP server at https://api.trooth.co/public/mcp
meters tools/call at 300 units every 60 seconds per caller (the OAuth
subject when a valid token is presented, otherwise the IP address), counted in one
store shared by every server instance; each tool call costs 1 to 4 units, as
https://trooth.co/.well-known/mcp.json lists. Over it: 429 with Retry-After giving the seconds
until units free up.

Generated from app/api by scripts/gen-openapi.mjs. check:openapi fails the build
when this document and the source disagree.

NetworkProfileV2.title: Trooth Network profile response, contract version 2
NetworkProfileV2.description: The body GET https://trooth.co/api/network/profile?q=<domain or slug> returns, as JSON Schema. This is the canonical shape: the route is tested against it on every push (tests/public-contract-schema.test.mjs) and the live route is checked against it after every deployment (scripts/verify-public-contract.mjs). The MCP tool trooth_public_trust_profile on api.trooth.co reads this body and writes its answer from it. Additions do not move the contract version and are not refused here; a removal, a rename or a change of meaning moves it, and a new file is published beside this one. What this schema deliberately refuses: any field named rating, rank, grade or confidence, because the contract carries none and a reader must not be able to find one. Canonical JSON Schema: https://trooth.co/schemas/network-profile.v2.schema.json; embedded here with its $defs as NetworkProfileV2_* components.

NetworkProfileV2_notFound.description: No published profile answers this query, or the query was refused. Not an error about the company; the Network does not hold it.

found.description: Always false in this branch: no published profile answers the query.

error.description: A short machine code for why nothing was returned (for example missing q, rate_limited, unsupported_contract_version, profile_read_unavailable). Absent when the Network simply holds no profile for the query.

message.description: The same reason as a sentence, when there is one.

contractVersion.description: The contract version this body follows.

ambiguous.description: True when q is a company name that several published companies carry (REQ-4-1629). No record was chosen; candidates lists what the name could mean. Additive in contract 2 (2026-09-29).

candidates.description: Present with ambiguous. Each published company the name could mean, ordered by slug (an order that suggests none), with the exact query that selects it.

slug.description: The company's slug on the Network.

domain.description: The company's domain, or null when none is published.

profileUrl.description: The company's public Trust Profile page.

select.description: Send this as q to read this company's record and no other.

candidatesTotal.description: How many published companies carry the name, when ambiguous.

candidatesTruncated.description: True when candidates lists fewer companies than candidatesTotal.

found.description: Always true in this branch: a published profile answers the query.

contractVersion.description: The contract version of this body. It moves only when a field is removed or renamed or a value changes meaning.

contractNote.description: What the contract version promises, as a sentence.

contractOmissions.description: Fields this contract deliberately does not carry, each with the reason, so a reader does not look for them.

deprecation.description: A notice when a field or this contract version is being retired; an empty string when nothing is.

sectionCapabilities.description: The section map: for each section of a company record, whether this full record, the bounded MCP summary, the profile Markdown and the directory entry carry it (supported), leave it out on purpose (omitted), cannot carry it yet (unavailable) or never carry it because it is private (unpublished). Static and free of company data. Absence in a projection is never a negative fact.

slug.description: The company's slug on the Network; send it as q to read the same record.

domain.description: The company's domain, or null when none is published.

canonicalUrl.description: The company's public Trust Profile page, the human-readable form of this record.

tagline.description: The company's one-line description, as the company wrote it, or null.

industries.description: Industries the company lists for itself.

updatedAt.description: When the company last published a change to this record. An ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, or null when none is recorded.

witnessed.description: What Trooth itself observed about the public surface. See the witnessBlock definition.

witnessStatement.description: The one signed object in this response. Absent (the key is not in the body) when the latest reading has no signed statement.

witnessEvidenceManifest.description: The evidence manifest the statement binds by digest. Present with a v2 statement.

methodology.description: How readings are taken and kept, and what they do not cover.

assuranceBoundary.description: Added 2026-10-12 (audit F-04). What this record does and does not establish. The statement is the same sentence the profile page, badge, exports and MCP answers carry.

statement.const: This record organizes source-linked information for a security review. It is not an audit, certification, or suitability decision.
statement.description: The boundary in one sentence, word for word the sentence every Trooth surface carries.

doesNotEstablish.description: What a Trooth record does not establish, one item each.

methodology.description: Where the method is described: https://trooth.co/methodology.

facts.description: Every fact in the selected sections, one per field, each with who said it (origin) and, in contract 2, typed provenance (claim) and record metadata (record). Not signed.

conflicts.description: Fields where sources gave different accounts, each account with its origin. Trooth does not choose between them.

signing.description: What in this response is signed, and how to check it yourself.

requestedContract.description: The contract the caller asked for with ?contract= or the Trooth-Contract header, or null when it asked for none. contractVersion is the contract that served the response. Additive in contract 2 (2026-09-26).

evidenceClasses.description: What each evidenceClass value means. Additive in contract 2 (2026-09-26).

authority.description: Domain control, registry match, representative authority and publication permission, each stated separately, and Trooth's own record of the domain claim in claim. Additive in contract 2 (2026-09-26); claim added 2026-10-07.

claim.description: Trooth's own record of the domain claim for the workspace that published this profile, as Trooth recorded it at claim time. Every field is null when nothing is recorded or the record could not be read. It shows control of the domain at claim time; it does not establish the legal entity or that a person may act for it. Absent on responses served before 2026-10-07.

method.description: The proof that confirmed control of the domain: dns_txt (Trooth's challenge TXT record at _trooth-challenge.<domain>), domain_email_code (a code sent to a mailbox at the domain) or identity_provider_sign_in (a sign-in through the company's identity provider at the domain). Null when no proof is recorded.

confirmed_at.description: When Trooth recorded the confirmation (ISO 8601), or null.

id.description: An opaque id for the person who attested at claim time that they may act for the company: the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 over a fixed label, the owner account id and the domain. It holds no personal data and is stable for this claim.

attested_at.description: When the person made the attestation (ISO 8601).

method.description: The proof that person completed for this claim, in the same words as claim.method.

representative.description: The person who attested at claim time that they may act for the company, or null when no attestation is recorded. An attestation is the person's own statement; Trooth does not collect evidence of corporate authority.

legalEntity.description: Added 2026-10-12 (audit F-05). The legal entity the company declared behind this domain: name, jurisdiction, registration identifier, register, its relationship to the domain and the evidence the company cites. Always company_declared and not_validated: Trooth has no registry connector and no authority-confirmation workflow, so nothing here carries a validated label, and domain control does not establish any of it.

state.description: declared when the company named an entity or a relationship; not_registered when it said it has no registration; not_declared when nothing is published.

entityName.description: The legal name the company published, or null.

jurisdiction.description: Where the company says the entity is registered, or null.

registrationId.description: The registration number as the company typed it, or null.

register.description: The register the company names, e.g. Companies House, or null.

registerRecordUrl.description: The register's own record as the company linked it, or null.

relationshipToDomain.description: Which case the entity is with respect to this domain, as the company declared it, or null when unstated.

relationshipLabel.description: The reader's words for relationshipToDomain, or null.

evidenceRef.description: A link the company supplied. Trooth has not read or validated it.

legalName.description: The entity's legal name, as declared.

jurisdiction.description: Its jurisdiction, as declared, or null.

registrationId.description: Its registration number, as declared, or null.

role.description: Its role in the group (parent, operating, subsidiary, branch_of), as declared, or null.

otherEntities.description: Other entities the company declared in its group structure.

validation.description: Always not_validated: no independent validation exists today.

provenance.description: Who said it and whether anyone checked: always company_declared and not_validated today.

declaredAt.description: Server time of the publish that declared the values shown, or null for a record published before declarations were kept. Never the time of the read.

registryMatch.description: What Trooth checks against a register: the authority model's registryMatch sentence.

trustCenter.description: Added 2026-10-16. The trust center page the company stated on its published profile, where it publishes its security and compliance documents (for example on SafeBase, Vanta, Drata, Conveyor, Whistic, TrustArc, Secureframe or OneTrust, or its own /trust page), or null when it stated none. The company's statement, not Trooth's finding: statedBy is always company. Trooth reads this page at each witnessed reading and records what the page named in the public record (trust_center), labeled as what the page said; Trooth does not read the documents behind it or check its claims.

url.description: The trust center link as the company stated it: an https URL of at most 500 characters, on any host. Under a links restriction it is replaced with a withheld marker like every other outbound link.

statedBy.description: Who stated the link. Always the company.

relationships.description: What a listed relationship does and does not establish. Additive in contract 2 (2026-09-26).

selection.description: Which part of the record this response carries (REQ-4-1630). sections is the list asked for with ?sections=, or "all". recordVersion is the profile update time the page belongs to. total is how many facts the selected sections hold, returned how many this page carries, and truncated says whether any were left out; when it is true, next is a cursor to send as ?after= for the rest, refused as stale if the company publishes a new version in between. conflicts carries only the disagreements about facts on this page, and a contested fact stays marked.

sections.description: The section ids asked for, or the word all.

recordVersion.description: The record version this page was read from. Use it with next to page through one version.

limit.description: Facts per page as served, at most 200.

truncated.description: True when more facts follow on another page.

next.description: The cursor for the next page, or null when this page is the last.

note.description: What this page holds, as a sentence.

factFreshnessStatuses.description: One sentence of meaning for each value of facts[].record.freshness.status.

current.description: The meaning of the freshness status current, as a sentence.

due.description: The meaning of the freshness status due, as a sentence.

stale.description: The meaning of the freshness status stale, as a sentence.

not_collected.description: The meaning of the freshness status not_collected, as a sentence.

unknown.description: The meaning of the freshness status unknown, as a sentence.

unavailable.description: The meaning of the freshness status unavailable, as a sentence.

disputed.description: The meaning of the freshness status disputed, as a sentence.

profile.description: The complete record in the order of the public page: every section with its state, provenance and meaning.

identity.description: Added 2026-10-16 (record contract, https://trooth.co/methodology#record-reading). Who this record is about.

legal_name.description: The legal name the company published, or null.

domain.description: The domain this record is keyed by, or null.

registry_identifier.description: The registration identifier the company published, or null.

note.const: This record is keyed by domain. It is about the company at this domain, not about similarly named companies.
note.description: The fixed note: the record is keyed by domain.

record_summary.description: Added 2026-10-16 (record contract, https://trooth.co/methodology#record-reading). The record at a glance.

record_version.description: The stored record version this body is, or null when it is not known on this load.

last_witnessed_at.description: When Trooth last witnessed the company, ISO 8601 with time zone, or null.

public_record.description: Facts read from a public record.

counts_by_provenance.description: Published facts counted by provenance word; never added together into one figure.

sections_not_published.description: Section ids not published (including sections the company hid).

sections_on_request.description: Section ids available on request only.

checks_read.description: Checks the latest signed witness statement read, or null without one.

checks_as_expected.description: Of those, the checks whose outcome was as expected, or null.

failed_checks.description: Every check the latest statement read as not as expected.

verify_command.description: The command that checks the signed witness statement on the reader's own machine.

buyer_questions.description: Added 2026-10-16 (record contract, https://trooth.co/methodology#record-reading). The twelve standard buyer questions, in the contract's order, answered only from the record's own fields.

question.description: The question, in the contract's words.

answer_state.description: answered, no, not_published or not_read; the three negatives are never shown as one another.

answer.description: Null when answer_state is not_published or not_read.

sentence.description: One self-contained sentence carrying subject, provenance, date and value; null when not answered.

provenance.description: The provenance word of the answer, or null.

as_of.description: The newest declaration time behind the answer, else the published version time; null when not answered.

anchor_url.description: The anchor on the canonical page.

fact_ids.description: The fact ids the answer is read from.

controls_not_in_place.description: Added 2026-10-16 (record contract, https://trooth.co/methodology#record-reading). Controls not yet in place, read from the company's Trust Center control register where Trooth holds it as data; empty with controls_not_in_place_state not_published otherwise.

control.description: The control, as the register names it.

status_note.description: Its state in the register's own words, with its target date or trigger.

source_url.description: The register page it is read from.

controls_not_in_place_state.description: Added 2026-10-16 (record contract, https://trooth.co/methodology#record-reading). published: the list is read from the company's own Trust Center register. not_published: no register is held for this company, so an empty list says nothing about its controls.

NetworkProfileV2_witnessBlock.description: What Trooth itself has observed about the company's public surface. `standing` is either the word `witnessed` or null; there is no third value and no degree. Null throughout means no observation was returned, which is not a finding about the company.

standing.description: The word witnessed: Trooth has a reading of this public surface. It is not a grade and has no degrees.

lastWitnessed.description: When the latest reading was taken. An ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, or null when none is recorded.

firstWitnessedAt.description: When the first reading of this company was taken. An ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, or null when none is recorded.

checksPassed.description: Checks read whose outcome was as expected. Part of checksRun, not a separate addend.

checksRun.description: Checks read in the latest reading.

source.description: What checksRun and checksPassed count. witness_statement: computed from the signed witness statement's entries; checksRun is checks read in this reading. result_tally: the reading's own tally for a reading with no statement; not a count of checks read. Additive in contract 2 (2026-09-26); absent on responses served before it.

definition.description: The same meaning, as a sentence.

checksNotRead.description: Entries in the reading that were not read in it. Present when source is witness_statement.

checksNotAsExpected.description: Entries read whose outcome was not as expected: checksRun minus checksPassed, so checksRun = checksPassed + checksNotAsExpected. Present when source is witness_statement. Additive (2026-09-28).

checksInReading.description: checksRun plus checksNotRead. Present when source is witness_statement.

coverage.description: What the latest reading counted, reported apart and never combined into one number; null when no counts are available.

recordBegan.description: When the reading series began. An ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, or null when none is recorded.

unbrokenSince.description: Since when readings have stayed within the gap tolerance. An ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, or null when none is recorded.

unbrokenReadings.description: Readings in the current unbroken series.

totalReadings.description: Readings kept in the retention window.

continuity.description: How long readings have run without a gap longer than methodology.gapTolerance.

standing.description: Null: no reading was returned. That is not a finding about the company.

lastWitnessed.description: Null when there is no reading.

firstWitnessedAt.description: Null when there is no reading.

coverage.description: Null when there is no reading.

continuity.description: Null when there is no reading.

NetworkProfileV2_witnessStatement.description: Trooth's signed statement of the reading behind `witnessed`, carried exactly as the upstream witness worker signed it. Present only when that reading was signed under the witness statement; absent (the key is not in the body) for an older reading, which is not a failed check. `payload` is the signing input itself: check the Ed25519 signature over its UTF-8 bytes with the key `key_id` names at https://api.trooth.co/public/keys, decoding that key by its `encoding`, then parse `payload` to read it. Two versions exist, named by the payload's own `statement` field. trooth.witness-statement.v2 (readings signed from 2026-10-04) carries `statement`, `reading_id`, `domain`, `read_at`, `subject_scope` (`domain`, `surface`, `checks_in_scope`), `methodology` (`standard`, `mapping_version`, `mapping_url`, `mapping_digest`: sha256 over the exact bytes of the immutable mapping file at https://trooth.co/standard/check-mapping/<version>.json), `evaluator` (`name`, `version`), `evidence_manifest` (`digest`, `entries`, `canonicalization`), `checks` (each with `id`, `category`, `kind`, an `outcome` of `as expected`, `not as expected` or `not read`, and for every outcome other than `as expected` a `reason` with a versioned `code`, a `source_ref` or an explicit `withheld` and `withheld_reason`) and `counts` (`read`, `as_expected`, `not_as_expected`, `not_read`, `in_reading`, with read + not_read = in_reading and as_expected + not_as_expected = read). A timeout or an unavailable source is `not read`, never `not as expected`. trooth.witness-statement.v1 (earlier readings) carries `statement`, `reading_id`, `domain`, `read_at`, `checks` (`id`, `category`, `kind`, `outcome`) and `counts` (`read`, `as_expected`). Its assurance is narrower: it shows the key signed those outcome bytes and does not bind the check mapping, the evaluator version, the subject scope or the evidence sources. No digest is ever added to a v1 statement. Neither version carries a verdict, a threshold or a composite figure. This is the only signed part of the body. Trooth signs what it witnessed. It never signs on a company's behalf.

payload.description: The exact string that was signed. Do not re-serialize it before checking.

signature.description: The prefix `ed25519:` followed by the standard base64 of the 64 signature bytes.

key_id.description: The `kid` of the signing key at https://api.trooth.co/public/keys.

canonicalization.description: How the worker serialized the payload before signing: JSON with keys in a fixed order and no whitespace, as UTF-8. `payload` is already in that form.

NetworkProfileV2_witnessEvidenceManifest.description: The evidence manifest a trooth.witness-statement.v2 statement binds through `evidence_manifest.digest`: one entry per check, each a public `source` reference or a `commitment` (sha256 over a secret salt, one 0x0a byte and a private reference) where publishing the reference would expose a company's declaration or a sensitive path. Recompute the digest as sha256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the entries sorted by `check_id` and serialized as JSON with keys `check_id` then `source` or `commitment` and no whitespace, and compare it to the signed digest. Additive (2026-10-04); present only beside a v2 statement, never beside v1, and not itself signed.

check_id.description: The check id in the mapping the statement names. Unique in the manifest.

source.description: The public URL the check read.

check_id.description: The check id in the mapping the statement names. Unique in the manifest.

commitment.description: sha256 over a secret salt, one 0x0a byte and the private reference; only the company holding it can open it.

NetworkProfileV2_methodology.description: How the witnessed block was produced and what it does not cover. Included in every response so a reader restating witnessed elsewhere can carry the limits with it.

cadence.description: How often readings are attempted, as a sentence.

gapTolerance.description: The longest gap between readings that still counts as unbroken, as a sentence.

retention.description: How long readings are kept, as a sentence.

window.description: How long an observation in this category stays current, as words (for example 48 hours).

freshness.description: For each category of fact, how long an observation stays current.

exclusions.description: What the readings do not cover, one sentence each.

summary.description: The methodology in one paragraph, for a reader restating witnessed elsewhere.

NetworkProfileV2_origin.description: Who said it. company-declared is the company's own statement; witnessed is Trooth's observation; public-source is a named third party. The order accounts are listed in is fixed and is not a ranking.

key.description: The stable field key, section.field (for example identity.legal-name).

category.description: The section the fact belongs to, as words.

value.description: The value as published, as text.

origin.description: Who said it: company-declared, witnessed or public-source.

contested.description: True when another source gave a different account; the accounts are in conflicts under the same key, and value is one of them, not the winner.

claim.description: Typed provenance for this claim, additive in contract 2 (2026-09-26). Fields Trooth does not hold are null and named in unknown; a claim never inherits the reading's time or signature.

claimId.description: The claim id: the domain, a # and the field key. Stable across record versions.

domain.description: The company domain the claim is about.

scope.description: Always company: the claim is about the company as a whole.

evidenceClass.description: company_declaration: the company said it. trooth_observation: Trooth read it from the public surface. public_record: a named outside source.

declaredAt.description: For a company declaration, the time an authorized publish on Trooth first carried the current value, or of a later publish at which an owner or admin declared every published fact again. Null for a fact published before Trooth began recording it, unchanged since and not declared again; never a profile version date or a reading time.

observedAt.description: When Trooth or a public source observed the value, or null. An ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, or null when none is recorded.

validUntil.description: When the claim stops applying, when the source states it; otherwise null.

evidenceRef.description: The reference a declared fact cites, as the company gave it, or null. Trooth has not opened it.

signed.description: Always false: a fact is not signed by anyone. The one signed object is witnessStatement.

issuerAuthenticated.description: True only when the publish that carried this value was accepted from a signed-in Trooth session whose workspace role was owner or admin, or from the workspace AI agent acting in such a session while its publishing permission was on. False for every other declaration, every observation and every public record. It is about the publishing session: it does not mean Trooth checked the statement, that a document issuer was authenticated, or that the person holds legal authority for the company. Before 2026-10-04 this field was always false.

unknown.description: Names of claim fields Trooth does not know for this fact; they are listed rather than guessed.

declaredBy.description: Additive (2026-10-04). Present only when declaredAt is set: the actor class and workspace role of the session that published the value. Absent otherwise. Carries no personal data.

actorClass.description: person or agent: what kind of signed-in actor published the value.

role.description: The publisher's role in the company workspace: owner, admin, editor, or unknown.

record.description: Per-fact identity, issuer, method version and freshness, additive in contract 2 (2026-09-29, REQ-4-1640 and REQ-4-1588). freshness.status tells seven answers apart instead of one null: current, due and stale are a dated observation against its category window; not_collected is a company statement Trooth does not re-read; unknown is an origin with no recorded observation time or an unreadable date; unavailable is a source not read on this pass; disputed means another account is in conflicts. Fields Trooth does not hold are null and explained in unknown.

companyId.description: The company's id on the Network (its slug).

recordVersion.description: The record version this fact was read from, or null.

sourceReference.description: Where the value can be read: the profile page for a declaration, the source for a public record.

collectedAt.description: Always null: the record keeps when a version was published, not when each field entered it.

methodVersion.description: The version of the method that produced this record entry.

status.description: One of the statuses explained in factFreshnessStatuses.

collection.description: How the value arrives: declared_by_company, read_by_trooth or public_source.

lastObservedAt.description: The last dated observation, or null. An ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, or null when none is recorded.

windowDays.description: The freshness window in days, or null when the value has none.

windowCategory.description: The methodology.freshness category that sets the window, or null.

nextExpectedRefresh.description: When a fresh observation is next expected, or null.

freshness.description: Whether the value is inside its category freshness window.

unknown.description: Record fields Trooth does not know for this fact, each with the reason.

fact_id.description: Added 2026-10-16 (record contract, https://trooth.co/methodology#record-reading). The stable fact id, <section>.<field>: the section name the .md, JSON and MCP surfaces share and the field's key in lower snake case; a list member adds .member.<member key>. Never contains the record version.

anchor_url.description: Added 2026-10-16 (record contract, https://trooth.co/methodology#record-reading). The fact's anchor on the canonical page: #fact-<fact_id with . written as ->.

sentence.description: Added 2026-10-16 (record contract, https://trooth.co/methodology#record-reading). One self-contained sentence: subject, provenance, date and value.

freshness_window.description: Added 2026-10-16 (record contract, https://trooth.co/methodology#record-reading). The methodology's freshness window for this fact as an ISO 8601 duration (P30D), or null when no window applies (a company statement Trooth does not re-read).

stale_after.description: Added 2026-10-16 (record contract, https://trooth.co/methodology#record-reading). When the fact's dated observation goes stale, ISO 8601 with time zone, or null.

witnessed_value.description: Trooth's own observation of the same claim, beside the declaration, or null.

edit_history.description: Added 2026-10-16 (record contract, https://trooth.co/methodology#record-reading). Declared facts only: the changes to this fact across the newest stored record versions (at most 25 versions), oldest first. Empty when none is held.

key.description: The field key the accounts disagree on.

accounts.description: Each account, with who gave it. Listed in a fixed order that is not a ranking.

NetworkProfileV2_signing.description: What in this response is signed. Additive in contract 2 (2026-09-26). profileSigned is always false: the one signed object is witnessStatement, which covers one reading and nothing else.

profileSigned.description: Always false: this response as a whole is not signed.

signedArtifact.description: The name of the one signed field, witnessStatement, or null when there is no statement.

artifactType.description: The signed statement's own type tag. With no statement, trooth.witness-statement.v1.

subject.description: What the signed statement covers and does not cover, as a sentence.

binding.description: What the statement binds (additive, 2026-10-04). null when there is no statement. `status` is `present` for v2 and `absent` for v1, whose assurance is narrower: v1 binds no mapping, evaluator version, scope or sources, and its digests here are null rather than filled in. A reader who receives the document under a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) hashes it and checks the result against the published digest. Trooth has not read the document and has not checked the digest. An item under "Attestation result (published by the company)" in the security section is a confidential-computing attestation result the company published: Platform, What runs in it, Verifier (named by the company), Appraised (an ISO date) and SHA-256 of the result (stated by the company), with the note that Trooth has not appraised the hardware evidence and has not checked the signature.

NetworkProfileV1.description: DEPRECATED. Contract 1 of the profile read, served only to a caller that pins it with ?contract=1 or the Trooth-Contract: 1 request header, together with Deprecation and Sunset response headers, until its withdrawal on 2027-03-01 (https://trooth.co/changelog). get.description: Full-text search over published company listings. Returns the same companies the public directory shows. Prefer cursor pagination: pass the returned next_cursor back as cursor. Offset pagination still works and is kept for clients that already ship with it, but it is deprecated: it counts rows rather than naming a position, so a directory that grows between two requests can serve the same company twice and skip another without erroring. A response to an offset-paged request carries a Deprecation header and a Link header with rel="deprecation"; no withdrawal date is set, so no Sunset header is sent. A cursor that cannot be read returns 400 rather than an empty page. Cached at the edge for 60 seconds with a 300 second stale-while-revalidate window. BEST-EFFORT, MUTABLE ENUMERATION: there is no snapshot. Every page reads the live directory, and the cursor names a position in the sort order, not a point in time; it is not bound to a snapshot, an as-of time or an expiry. A company whose witnessed state changes between two pages can be missed or returned twice, so a walk is not a consistent full export. Drop repeats by slug and walk again to reconcile. The fact pages of /api/network/profile are a different mechanism: their cursor is bound to one record version. Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

parameters.description: Search terms. Matched against company name and description.

parameters.name: industry
parameters.description: Restrict to one industry.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Results per page. Clamped to 100; anything unreadable falls back to 25.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque page marker. Use next_cursor from the previous response. Preferred over offset. It names a position in a live list, not a snapshot: it carries no as-of time and no expiry.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based offset. Use next_offset from the previous response. Deprecated in favor of cursor; still answered, with a Deprecation header on the response.

400.description: A cursor that cannot be read.

503.description: The directory could not be read. Not a statement about any company.

Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

503.description: The directory could not be read.

A slug of the form d--example.com resolves a witnessed company that has not yet published a rich profile. Cached at the edge for 120 seconds. Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

parameters.description: Company slug, or d--<domain>.

503.description: The record could not be read. Not a statement about the company.

get.description: The buyer-facing projection of a company's evidence: the witnessed state per area (the pillars key), provider status with the time each connected system was last read. Framework rollups were retired on 2026-09-26 and the frameworks array is always empty. Individual control rows, owners and internal notes are never returned here. Each pillar carries observedAt and sourceRef, null when Trooth holds no per-area read time or reference, or when the area is restricted: null reads as unknown and is never filled from another area, a provider sync or the company's last edit. Responds 404 when the company has no public record, which is a privacy-preserving answer rather than an error. This is the read the embeddable badge performs. Cached at the edge for 300 seconds. Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

parameters.description: Company handle.

404.description: No public record for this handle.

503.description: The record could not be read. Not a statement about the company.

get.summary: One company's canonical profile and witness facts
get.description: The canonical published profile for a company, keyed by domain or slug, with the witness facts a buyer's tool needs: the `standing` field (the witnessed state), lastWitnessed (freshness), firstWitnessedAt and the unbroken run of Trooth's own hourly readings (continuity), and checksPassed out of checksRun on the signed result (coverage: checks that read as expected, out of checks run). Continuity is never claimed older than Trooth's own record and stays null until two consecutive readings agree. Responds { found: false } with 200 when no profile is published, 400 when q is missing. Cached at the edge for 120 seconds. Every response carries a `methodology` object stating the reading cadence, the gap tolerance that defines an unbroken series, the retention period, the per-category freshness windows, and an explicit list of coverage limits - what Trooth does not read. A caller restating `witnessed` or `updatedAt` elsewhere must carry those limits with it: neither field is a certification nor an audit opinion. Only the witness statement is signed; the profile, its facts and the company's text are not (see `signing`). `sectionCapabilities` links the section map, which says which sections this record and the other projections carry. Limited to 600 requests a minute and 20,000 an hour per client network (an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 /64), counted across server instances; over either window the answer is 429 with Retry-After set to the seconds until that window resets. If the counting store fails, each instance counts alone at the same ceilings and the read is not refused. Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Company domain (example.com) or Trooth slug.

parameters.name: contract
parameters.description: Pin the response contract version, here or in the Trooth-Contract request header (not both with different values, which is refused with 400). Omit for the current contract. A version this deployment does not answer is refused with 400 rather than approximated. Every response names the contract that served it in the Trooth-Contract response header and in contractVersion, and the one requested in requestedContract; a request for contract 1 is served contract 1 itself, with Deprecation and Sunset headers, until its withdrawal on 2027-03-01, leaving out every fact two sources answered differently and naming each in withheldContested.

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: Comma-separated categories to return facts from: identity, registration, hosting, pricing, pricing-add-ons, security, privacy, privacy-roles, recovery, ai-practices. Omit for all. An unknown name is refused with 400 and the valid list; a section's conflicts travel with its facts.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Facts per page, 1 to 200. With limit or after, a page carries up to 100 facts unless limit says otherwise; with neither, the response carries every fact in the selected sections. The response's selection object says how many facts the selected sections hold, how many this page carries and whether it was truncated.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The selection.next cursor from the previous page. It is bound to the record version and to the sections asked for: if the company publishes a new version between pages, the cursor is refused with 400 (stale_cursor) rather than served from a different record. A cursor also expires 24 hours after the page that issued it and is then refused with 400 (cursor_expired).

200.description: The record, or { found: false } when the Network holds none. Which body is served is keyed by the Trooth-Contract response header: 2 (the default) is NetworkProfileV2, written to the published JSON Schema https://trooth.co/schemas/network-profile.v2.schema.json and validated against it on every push and after every deployment; 1 is NetworkProfileV1, deprecated, served only to a caller that pinned contract 1, with Deprecation and Sunset headers, until its withdrawal on 2027-03-01.

Trooth-Contract.description: The contract that served this body: 2, or 1 for a caller that pinned it.

Deprecation.description: Sent only with contract 1 (RFC 9745): contract 1 is deprecated.

Sunset.description: Sent only with contract 1 (RFC 8594): the date contract 1 is withdrawn, 2027-03-01, as an HTTP date.

ETag.description: A weak tag of this representation; send it back in If-None-Match for a 304.

schema.description: NetworkProfileV2 when Trooth-Contract is 2, NetworkProfileV1 when it is 1. The two never both match: contract 1 carries contractVersion 1 and no conflicts.

400.description: The q parameter is missing, a contract version this deployment does not answer was requested, the query and the Trooth-Contract header asked for different contracts, a section name or limit could not be applied exactly, or an after cursor is malformed, stale or was issued for other sections.

429.description: Over the per-network budget. Retry-After is the number of seconds until the window that refused resets.

503.description: Trooth could not read its own record on this load. Retry after the Retry-After interval; nothing is asserted about the company.

get.description: Multi-criteria discovery over the same published companies the directory lists: free text, industry, HQ country, data residency region, deployment model, product name, whether Trooth holds a witnessed reading, and profile changes since a date. A company is matched only by facts its public page shows: residency and deployment are searchable only while the company shows the section that renders them. Filters are exact, case-insensitive matches on what the company published; a company that published nothing for a filtered field is absent from the answer, which is not a no. Order is the directory's: witnessed first, then the most recent reading, then name; never by a figure. Each result carries facts, whole days counted from timestamps on the record (days_since_last_witnessed, days_since_profile_updated), which rate nothing. Cursor pagination only; a cursor is bound to the filters it was issued with. An unknown filter is refused. Errors are always RFC 9457 problem details (codes at /api/problems). Cached at the edge for 60 seconds with a 300 second stale-while-revalidate window. Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text, matched against name, tagline, domain, industries and product names.

parameters.name: industry
parameters.description: An industry, matched as a substring of the company's industries.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: The HQ country, as the company published it; exact, case-insensitive.

parameters.name: residency
parameters.description: A data residency region, as companies write it (EU, US, UK...); exact, case-insensitive.

parameters.name: hosting
parameters.description: A deployment model (Cloud, Private cloud / VPC, On-prem, Hybrid); exact, case-insensitive.

parameters.name: product
parameters.description: A product name, matched as a substring of the visible offering section.

parameters.name: witnessed
parameters.description: true for companies with a witnessed reading, false for those without.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: Only companies whose profile changed at or after this ISO 8601 date or UTC time.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Results per page, 1 to 100 (default 25).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: next_cursor from the previous page, sent with the same filters.

400.description: An unknown filter, a value that cannot be used, or a cursor issued for different filters.

503.description: The directory could not be read. Not an empty result.

post.summary: Check many companies in one call
post.description: A read of up to 25 companies in one request, for an agent that plans a sequence of steps and needs to know, before acting, what each company's record says and whether it changed since planning. Each target is a domain or profile slug, or { q, pin } where pin is the record digest from an earlier read. Each result has status (listed, not_listed, withheld, unavailable), what Trooth's own readings show, the version and SHA-256 digest of the record GET /api/network/profile serves, pin.changed when a pin was sent, and plain day counts. A target that cannot be read is that target's unavailable, with the problem registry's retryable flag and next action; the other targets are still answered. It changes nothing, so it takes no Idempotency-Key and repeating it is always safe. Nothing in it grades, ranks or certifies a company. Errors are always RFC 9457 problem details. Never cached. Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

targets.description: Domains or profile slugs, each a string or { q, pin }.

pin.description: The record digest from an earlier read.

200.description: One result per target, in the order sent.

400.description: The body or a target cannot be used; errors[] points into the body.

413.description: The body is larger than 16 KiB.

get.summary: Every record version across the Network
get.description: Every published record version across the Trooth Network after a position, oldest first, at most 100 per page: the company, the version, its SHA-256 digest and the previous one, and where to read it. No record body and no personal fact. Without after or since, the page starts 24 hours back. next is the cursor to send as after, and also the id of the last event, so a client can move between this feed and the event stream without losing its place. Order is by recorded time, ties broken by event id; delivery is at least once across a reconnect (drop repeats by event_id); a company that withdraws its profile stops appearing. A position older than the retention window is 410 beyond_retention. Errors are always RFC 9457 problem details. Never cached. Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: next from the previous page, or an event id from the stream.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Start at this ISO 8601 date or UTC time instead of a cursor.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Events per page, 1 to 100 (default 50).

400.description: A position or limit that cannot be used.

410.description: The position is older than the feed keeps (beyond_retention); read the records in full and resume from a fresh position.

503.description: The feed could not be read, or history is not set up on this database.

get.summary: Every record version, as Server-Sent Events
get.description: The change feed as a text/event-stream (WHATWG Server-Sent Events). Each event is event: record.version, with the same JSON an entry of GET /api/network/changes carries and id set to its cursor, so a client that reconnects with Last-Event-ID (every EventSource does) resumes exactly after the last event it received. Without Last-Event-ID or after, the stream starts now. A connection is held for about 50 seconds and closed with a comment; the client reconnects (retry: 3000). A comment is sent every 15 seconds on a quiet stream. Errors before the stream opens are RFC 9457 problem details. Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The id of the last event received; the stream resumes after it.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The same as Last-Event-ID, for a client that cannot set headers.

200.description: An event stream of record.version events.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events; each data line is a NetworkChanges_event.

400.description: A position that cannot be read.

410.description: The position is older than the feed keeps.

503.description: The feed could not be read, or history is not set up.

get.summary: Every error code and whether retrying can help
get.description: The registry every RFC 9457 problem document from trooth.co draws on: each code with its status, fixed title, retryable flag, next action, and terminal (true when repeating the same request cannot change the answer, exactly not retryable). A code keeps its meaning once published. Cached for one hour. Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

Name-to-company suggestions for a search box, over the same published listings the directory shows. Cached at the edge for 60 seconds. Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Partial company name.

get.description: The full text of one of the twenty published Trooth legal documents, with its title, effective date and body. The slug must be one of the published set; anything else responds 404. Cached at the edge for one hour with a one day stale-while-revalidate window. Readable cross-origin: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a browser on any site may read it without cookies.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Document slug, for example privacy, terms, subprocessors.
